symptoms: Payment API response time increased from 200ms to 4 seconds during peak checkout traffic.
resolution: Validated pool utilization and active sessions, then adjusted pool limits and restarted affected application instances.

symptoms: Intermittent payment failures during peak traffic with elevated database CPU.
root_cause: Database CPU utilization exceeded 90 percent due to unindexed transaction history queries.
resolution: Reviewed query plans, added an index after validation, and increased database capacity for the peak window.

symptoms: Users experienced login failures and authentication requests timed out.
root_cause: Authentication service memory pressure caused repeated worker restarts.
resolution: Compared heap and worker metrics, fixed a token cache retention issue, and restarted affected instances.

symptoms: Order creation requests returned HTTP 500 errors after a release.
root_cause: A deployment introduced an incompatible API dependency.
resolution: Rolled back the release and restored the prior dependency after confirming the error rate declined.

symptoms: Payment requests showed increased latency after a new application release.
root_cause: Inefficient serialization code introduced during deployment increased request CPU time.
resolution: Compared release performance, rolled back the change, and deployed a corrected version after review.

symptoms: Email notifications were delayed and the worker queue backlog grew steadily.
root_cause: A downstream email provider rate limit caused retries to accumulate.
resolution: Checked provider response codes, applied bounded backoff, and drained the backlog gradually.

symptoms: Search requests returned intermittent 503 responses and elevated latency.
root_cause: Search cluster shard allocation was constrained after one node became unavailable.
resolution: Verified cluster health and disk capacity, restored the node, and monitored shard recovery.

symptoms: Available stock values differed between checkout and the inventory endpoint.
root_cause: A delayed event consumer left the read model behind the source of truth.
resolution: Compared event offsets, resumed the consumer after validating replay safety, and reconciled affected records.

symptoms: Label creation requests timed out while calls to a carrier integration were slow.
root_cause: Carrier API response time exceeded the client timeout and saturated outbound workers.
resolution: Reviewed carrier status and worker saturation, then used bounded concurrency and retry limits.

symptoms: Scheduled report generation missed its completion window.
root_cause: A large report query scanned an unpartitioned date range and exceeded its job time budget.
resolution: Reviewed query plan and job duration, narrowed the date range, and scheduled the heavier report off peak.

symptoms: Users were intermittently logged out after token refresh requests failed.
root_cause: Clock skew between application instances and the identity provider caused token validation failures.
resolution: Compared synchronized timestamps and token expiry claims, corrected time synchronization, and monitored refresh success.

symptoms: Product detail requests returned stale prices for a subset of items.
root_cause: Cache invalidation events were dropped during a brief message broker reconnect.
resolution: Checked broker offsets and cache age, replayed safe invalidation events, and verified values against the source database.

symptoms: Order status updates stopped appearing in the customer portal.
root_cause: The order event consumer exhausted its database write connections after a retry loop.
resolution: Inspected consumer logs and connection metrics, bounded retries, and resumed processing after clearing the stuck batch.

symptoms: A small number of payment requests were rejected with gateway errors while the API health check remained available.
root_cause: An upstream payment gateway returned transient 502 responses.
resolution: Compared gateway response codes and request IDs, checked provider status, and verified bounded retry behavior.

symptoms: Image upload requests failed when uploaded files were larger than the configured limit.
root_cause: The reverse proxy body-size limit was lower than the documented client upload limit.
resolution: Compared proxy and application limits, aligned the setting with the product requirement, and validated representative uploads.
